llm.summary: This is a disclosed VMware audit and policy helper that stores local audit/config files and does not show hidden exfiltration, destructive behavior, or deceptive instructions.

dimensions.detail: It reads selected agent-identifying environment variable presence and supports OPS_HOME and VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED; these are documented, limited to local policy/audit behavior, and do not include API-key harvesting.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation uses uv for the vmware-policy package and the docs disclose standalone and dependency installation paths; no bundled scripts, remote execution snippets, or hidden install hooks were found in the inspected artifact files.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill is auto-loaded as a dependency for VMware tools and may sit in sensitive workflows, but that role is disclosed and aligned with its audit/policy infrastructure purpose.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: It creates local ~/.vmware audit, rules, and undo state with restrictive permissions; this persistence is disclosed and purpose-aligned, though audit logs can contain sensitive operational details and policy checks fail open if audit writes fail.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is audit logging, policy checks, and response sanitization for VMware skill-family tools; the artifacts consistently describe a Python library and CLI with no MCP tools of its own.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this only if you use the VMware skill family and are comfortable with local audit records under ~/.vmware. Configure rules.yaml for production restrictions, protect audit.db because it may contain operational details, and do not leave VMWARE_POLICY_DISABLED set except for deliberate break-glass use.
llm.findings:
[PE3] expected: The kubeconfig/token/password references are redaction examples and sensitive-result handling guidance, not evidence of credential-file reading or credential theft in the artifact text.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad dependency activation is real, but it is disclosed as infrastructure used by VMware skills and does not itself expose MCP tools or hidden administrative actions.
[PE2] expected: The chmod examples set restrictive permissions on the local ~/.vmware directory and audit database; they are not sudo/root execution or privilege escalation.
[RA2] expected: The local ~/.vmware state, audit.db, rules.yaml, and undo.db are persistent, but they are documented audit/config stores rather than unauthorized services, startup hooks, or background persistence.
[EA2] expected: The default policy allowing all operations unless user rules are configured is a safety limitation, but it is explicitly documented and VMware authorization still depends on the underlying vCenter/NSX account RBAC.
[E3] expected: The ls command only checks the configured ~/.vmware/rules.yaml file timestamp during troubleshooting and is not broad filesystem enumeration.
[A.I.G SARIF] expected: The supplied A.I.G scan reported no results and a 100 security score for the Markdown artifact set.
